issue.title: Record the decision that saved capture templates are bob-owned and checked out, not popped
issue.description: Proposed by bob-cli-8b.2 note #1, bob-cli-8b.3 note #1, and bob-cli-8b.5 note #1 (epic bob-cli-8b, plan plan:202610/saved_capture_templates.md). The epic's auto decision `memory_saved_templates_decision = no` skipped this record, so no memory was changed in the epic. This bead is the decision-record half; the glossary strand is a separate task. Small: one fully specified strand from the accepted plan, not new design work.

task_type_fields.proposed_change: Add an accepted decisions strand `decisions:saved-templates-are-checked-out` (use `/sase_memory_write`). Claim: saved capture templates are a bob-owned shelf of `@@template:` blocks (never rows) at `$XDG_STATE_HOME/bob-cli/capture/templates.json`, saved by `bob capture` only after a successful real template capture; a Bob Mac Capture Control-T pick is a checkout (origin held in app memory) that a successful capture settles by replace-by-origin (`--template-origin`) in one locked write, and abandoning leaves the original untouched. Alternatives rejected: a Mac-owned store (violates `decisions:mac-capture-is-a-thin-client`), a literal pop (the only copy vanishes on Discard/Control-C/quit/crash), and saving as a staged participant in the vault commit (see the research report's "Resolving the disagreements"). Cost: an edited checkout stashed with Control-C lands beside the original rather than replacing it. Reopens when cross-machine reuse, template names, or pinning are needed. Cite epic bob-cli-8b, plan:202610/saved_capture_templates.md, and research:202610/capture_template_shelf/capture_template_shelf.md.

issue.creation_reason: Three bob-cli-8b phases proposed this record after the epic's auto decision skipped it; the shelf/checkout design now ships with no decisions strand governing it.
